newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Rabobank starts MOL coverage with 'hold'.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank starts MOL coverage with 'hold'.

text.p: Rabobank Investment Ltd started coverage of Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt with a 'hold' recommendation.

"The valuation of the company seems high compared to other international producers but we believe that this is appropriate given that MOL is the most liquid and largest capitalised stock on the exchange," said analysts Anthony Vago and Rupert Foster.
In a report they added that the outlook for the Hungarian market was positive.
The analysts expected MOL's earnings per share to be to 218.9 forints in 1997 and 229.8 forints in 1998.
They said MOL's gas business would hardly add to the company's profits in the coming years.

"The gas business is forecast to at best only break even in the next two years because of declining domestic production capacity and the gas price rises provided for by the gas pricing formula will not be high enough," they said.
MOL's CEO Zoltan Mandoki said in late June that last year MOL's gas business was 12.6 billion forints in the red while in the first half of 1997 the loss would be around seven billion forints.
Rabobank Investment Ltd is the securities arm of Rabobank Hungaria, which is a unit of Rabobank Nederland.
